issues.label: Interpretation of subsection 83(3) of the Regulations
Disposition of appeal and judicial review application

result.overall: The Federal Court of Appeal allowed the Minister's appeal, finding that the visa officer correctly interpreted subsection 83(3) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations to require completion of a single two-year full-time program at a post-secondary institution in Canada, and that the officer's decision was reasonable on the facts.

themes.name: Interpretation of subsection 83(3) of the Regulations
themes.summary: The Court considered whether adaptability points for Canadian study can be awarded by aggregating multiple shorter programs or require completion of a single two-year full-time program.

themes.name: Standard of review
themes.summary: The Court determined the appropriate standard of review for the visa officer's interpretation of the Regulations and application to facts.

themes.name: Application of subsection 83(3) to facts (reasonableness)
themes.summary: The Court assessed whether the visa officer reasonably applied the correct interpretation of subsection 83(3) to Mr. Patel's study history.

themes.name: Disposition of appeal and judicial review application
themes.summary: The Court decided to allow the Minister's appeal, dismiss the judicial review application, and answered the certified question negatively.

arguments.quote: He claimed 74 selection points, including five points for adaptability based upon his two years of Canadian post-secondary study.
arguments.claim: Mr. Patel claimed five adaptability points for two years of Canadian post-secondary study.

arguments.quote: A visa officer refused Mr. Patel’s application for permanent residence on the basis that his application merited only 63 selection points - four less than the required 67 points.
arguments.claim: The visa officer refused the application for not meeting the minimum points, awarding no adaptability points.

arguments.quote: The Judge certified the following serious question of general importance: In assessing adaptability under s. 83 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations, should a visa officer aggregate programs of study that do not each constitute two years of full-time study of at least two years’ duration at a post-secondary institution in Canada and award points if the total period of study amounts to or exceeds two years of full-time study at one or more post-secondary institutions?
arguments.claim: The Federal Court certified a question about whether adaptability points can be awarded by aggregating multiple shorter programs.

arguments.quote: The Judge rejected the Minister’s argument that the appropriate standard of review to be applied to the officer’s decision was reasonableness.
arguments.claim: The Federal Court Judge held the standard of review for the visa officer's interpretation of section 83 was correctness, but reasonableness for mixed fact and law.

arguments.quote: The Judge found the officer interpreted section 83 so as to require full-time attendance for two years in a single academic program at a single accredited institution.
arguments.claim: The Federal Court Judge found the visa officer erred by requiring study in a single program at one institution.
arguments.outcome_note: The Court disagreed with the Judge's interpretation and upheld the visa officer's interpretation.

arguments.quote: The Minister argues that the visa officer’s interpretation of the Regulations should have been reviewed on the standard of reasonableness.
arguments.claim: The Minister argued the visa officer's interpretation should be reviewed on a reasonableness standard.
arguments.outcome_note: The Court held the standard of review for interpretation is correctness.
arguments.quote_snapped: 127 at paragraph 34, argues that the visa officer’s interpretation of the Regulations should have been reviewed on the standard of reasonableness.

arguments.quote: The respondent replies that the standard of review is correctness and that the Judge correctly found the officer’s interpretation of the Regulations to be wrong.
arguments.claim: The respondent argued the standard of review is correctness and the visa officer's interpretation was wrong.
arguments.outcome_note: The Court disagreed and upheld the visa officer's interpretation.

arguments.quote: The officer viewed subsection 83(3) of the Regulations to require study at a post-secondary Canadian institution in a single program of full-time study of at least two years’ duration.
arguments.claim: The visa officer interpreted subsection 83(3) to require completion of a single two-year full-time program at one institution.

arguments.quote: The officer expressed concern that Mr. Patel had completed a one-year program of study at one school and then completed one semester at a different school.
arguments.claim: The officer noted Mr. Patel's studies were in two distinct programs at different institutions, not a single two-year program.
arguments.quote_snapped: Patel had completed a one-year program of study at one school and then completed one semester at a different school.

holdings.quote: I would allow the appeal, dismiss Mr. Patel’s application for judicial review and answer the certified question in the negative.
holdings.statement: The Court allowed the Minister's appeal, dismissed the judicial review application, and answered the certified question negatively.

holdings.quote: The standard of appellate review is whether the Judge of the Federal Court selected the appropriate standard of review and then applied it correctly.
holdings.statement: On appeal from judicial review, the appellate court reviews whether the lower court selected and applied the correct standard of review.

holdings.quote: A visa officer’s interpretation of the Act or the Regulations is reviewable on the standard of correctness.
holdings.statement: Visa officers' interpretations of legislation are reviewed on a correctness standard.

holdings.quote: The Judge did not err by reviewing the visa officer’s interpretation of subsection 83(3) of the Regulations on the standard of correctness.
holdings.statement: The Federal Court Judge correctly applied the correctness standard to the visa officer's interpretation of subsection 83(3).

holdings.quote: Interpreting subsection 83(3) of the Regulations to require study at a post-secondary Canadian institution in one program for at least two years is consistent with the plain meaning of both the English and French versions of the text.
holdings.statement: The plain language of subsection 83(3) supports requiring completion of a single two-year full-time program.

holdings.quote: Such an interpretation is also consistent with the statutory context and the purpose of the legislation.
holdings.statement: The legislative purpose supports requiring completion of one program rather than aggregating disparate programs for adaptability points.

holdings.quote: The Judge erred in law when he found the visa officer incorrectly interpreted subsection 83(3) of the Regulations.
holdings.statement: The Judge erred in concluding the visa officer's interpretation of subsection 83(3) was incorrect.

holdings.quote: The visa officer’s decision falls within a range of possible, acceptable outcomes which are defensible in respect of the facts and the law.
holdings.statement: The visa officer reasonably applied subsection 83(3) to the facts and made a defensible decision.

rebuttals.quote: The Judge rejected the Minister’s argument that the appropriate standard of review to be applied to the officer’s decision was reasonableness.
rebuttals.point: The Minister argued the standard of review should be reasonableness.
rebuttals.court_answer: The Judge held the interpretation of section 83 is a question of law reviewed on correctness, not reasonableness.

rebuttals.quote: The Minister argues that the visa officer’s interpretation of the Regulations should have been reviewed on the standard of reasonableness.
rebuttals.point: The Minister argued the visa officer's interpretation should be reviewed on reasonableness standard.
rebuttals.court_answer: The Court rejected this and held the standard of review for interpretation is correctness.
rebuttals.quote_snapped: 127 at paragraph 34, argues that the visa officer’s interpretation of the Regulations should have been reviewed on the standard of reasonableness.

rebuttals.quote: The respondent replies that the standard of review is correctness and that the Judge correctly found the officer’s interpretation of the Regulations to be wrong.
rebuttals.point: The respondent argued the standard of review is correctness and the visa officer's interpretation was wrong.
rebuttals.court_answer: The Court rejected the respondent's position and upheld the visa officer's interpretation as correct.
